title: Skald: Norse and Viking Sound Effects
shortText: 125 viking SFX: shield wall, 10 war horn signals, 8 runes x 3 phases, the raid, the feast, 5 loops. WAV + OGG.
html:
The Norse saga, as one sound

125 viking and Norse sound effects in WAV and OGG for any game engine (Unity, Unreal, Godot, GameMaker, RPG Maker and HTML5): the shield wall as a system, 10 war horn signals, 8 Elder Futhark runes with a charge, a release and a fizzle each, seidr staffs and bone charms, the raid on a village, the longhouse feast, the Dane axe, the seax and the thrown axe and spear, hacksilver rewards, a carved wood and runestone interface, accents and 5 ambience loops. Royalty free for commercial games, no credit required. A free demo of 19 sounds is on this page.

Licence, up front

Royalty free. Commercial use. No attribution required. Use it in as many games as you like, on any platform. The one thing you may not do is resell or redistribute the sounds themselves as a sound pack. The plain language terms ship as LICENSE.txt, with a copy and paste credit line for anyone who wants one. Everything is synthesised from code, so there is no upstream sample licence behind it.

Hear it first

There is a free demo on this page: 19 sounds copied unaltered from the paid files. All five war horn signals, the shield wall in every state, the fire rune in all three phases, five interface cues and the longhouse at night.

One saga, one palette

Every sound is built from the materials of a Norse world: oak plank, linden shield boards under rawhide, forged iron, the seax blade, bone and antler, a drinking horn, cut hacksilver, amber, a granite runestone, pine, beach shingle and fire. Indoors is one timber longhouse; outdoors is the fjord, with the cliffs answering back. A viking game stops borrowing a generic medieval kit.

The war horn, as signals

Every horn file is one blast at one pitch: a lip buzzed horn that scoops into its note and may sag as the breath runs out, never a tune. Five signals climb from a short call to a long held blast, so a game can wire the rung to how urgent the order is, and five more name the orders: a rally, an advance, a retreat, a distant call from across the fjord and an answering call.

The shield wall, and the rest, as whole lifecycles

  • Shield wall: raise, lock, brace, break, reform
  • Longhouse door: bar drop, batter, break
  • Thatched roof: catch, burn (loop), roof collapse
  • Pitch torch: light, throw, land
  • Longship keel: ground, drag
  • Drinking horn: toast, set down
  • Dane axe: heft, swing
  • Seax: draw, stab

Plus the shield wall pushing at four strengths, each brighter than the last, two shield bashes and two rim splinters. No two states of one mechanism are the same sound renamed (23 pairs measured from the shipped files, 0 alike).

Eight runes, every phase

  • Kenaz, fire: the torch rune: a spark caught in pine pitch and flung as a sheet of flame.
  • Isa, ice: the ice rune: frost cracking across iron and a shard of ice thrown.
  • Thurisaz, thunder: the thunder rune: the air drawn tight, one crack of thunder and its roll along the fjord.
  • Algiz, ward: the elk rune of protection: a dome of air closing over the caster with a low wooden thrum.
  • Sowilo, sun: the sun rune: a gathering hiss of light loosed as one blinding beam.
  • Hagalaz, hail: the hail rune: a burst of hailstones rattling off shields, iron and timber.
  • Laguz, tide: the water rune: a wave drawn up off the fjord and broken over the foe.
  • Berkano, healing: the birch rune: a soft rush of leaves and a warm wooden ring that mends.

Each rune ships a charge, a release and a fizzle, so a magic system can wire the hold, the hit and the cancel. Checked from the shipped files, not promised: across the rune by phase grid the rune changes the sound and so does the phase (108 pairs, 0 alike). Wiring it is one string: kenaz_fire_charge, thurisaz_thunder_release.

7 ladder steps (the horn signals and the push strengths) measured from the shipped files, failing steps: 0.

The rest of the saga

  • 9 seidr sounds: an iron shod staff tapped on the floor, bone charms rattled, a spirit wind, rune lots cast onto a hide (two takes each) and a seidr trance loop.
  • 12 raid sounds: a door barred, battered (two takes) and broken in, thatch catching, burning as a loop and falling in, a pitch torch lit, thrown and landing, and the keel grounding on shingle and dragged up the beach.
  • 7 feast sounds: drinking horns knocked together and set down, mead poured, a hearth log falling, a trencher set down and fists on the table (two takes). Events, not a crowd.
  • 10 weapon sounds: the Dane axe hefted and swung, the seax drawn from its sheath and stabbed, and the axe and spear thrown (two takes each).
  • 8 rewards: hacksilver (two takes), an arm ring, amber, a rune unlocked, a saga entry carved, a hoard revealed and a loot chest opened.
  • 15 interface sounds: menu open and close on a runestone, select, confirm, cancel, error, tab, a leather pouch inventory, a hide map, quest update, save, equip and cursor takes.
  • 6 encounter and turn cues and 5 accents: discovery, danger, an omen, an oath sworn on the ring and the fallen, every one a single gesture, never a melody.
  • 5 ambience loops: a longhouse at night, the fjord shore at dawn, a runestone circle in the wind, a village burning in a raid and a winter camp (no storm).

Fit

  • WAV and OGG for every file, 16 bit, 44.1 kHz, mono, with a naming manifest listing every file by group.
  • 7 seamless loops with loop points in both formats, and none on a one shot.
  • 14 variation sets whose takes differ in length and in brightness.
  • One loudness band: the inner 80 percent of the pack sits inside 0.96 dB, so a war horn and a carved wood cursor share a mix.
  • Import notes for Unity, Unreal, Godot, GameMaker, RPG Maker and the web, and pack_proof.json with a sha256 and a measurement for every file: 1143 checks, 0 failed.

Already own our other sound packs?

Every file here was measured against every file in the studio's 6 nearest packs (medieval impacts, the naval battle, survival, place beds and two other era suites: 89500 pairs, on spectral shape and on envelope, each tolerant of a transposition): 89500 of 89500 are separate sounds. The proof ships in the download as cross_pack_proof.json.

Honest limits

These are synthesised sounds designed for games, not field recordings of a real war horn or a real longship: oak, linden, iron, bone, antler, horn, silver, amber, granite, pine, shingle, ice, water and fire. The figures above are signal measurements, not a claim that anything sounds good; that is what the free demo is for. There are no voices and no music: no war cries, no chants, no singing, and every horn signal is one blast at one pitch.

AI disclosure, stated truthfully: the code that generates these sounds was written with AI assistance. The sounds themselves are self contained procedural synthesis by Core Systems Asset Factory, with no generative audio model at any point. The cover is an AI generated illustration, and the store plates are drawn by AI written code from the pack's own waveforms.

More from the same studio

  • Longships, a Norse saga music pack, for the score these sounds play under.
  • Steel and Bone, medieval combat impacts by weapon and target, for the axe on the shield itself.
  • Leeward 02: The Sea Fight, the naval battle, for the raid's crossing.
  • Sixfold, elemental spell casting chains, for a wider spellbook.
  • Jianghu and Sengoku, the same idea for other eras: one era, one palette.
